decisive_items: Cone-beam computed tomography demonstrated radiolucent resorptive lesions cervically on the palatal aspects of teeth #11 and #21, originating from the external palatal surface and perforating into the pulp space
the lesion’s projection remained in the same position relative to the canal and that the canal outline was undisturbed
periapical radiographs of the maxillary central incisors revealed cervical areas of rarefaction
response.rationale: The localized palatal lesions arising from the external surface with an undisturbed canal projection identify external cervical resorption as the primary diagnostic process; the pulpal diagnosis is secondary to this resorption.

rejected.why: Generalized periodontal disease is present but does not explain the localized cervical resorptive defects or their unchanged canal projection.
